title: Multiple choice & summary completion
title_target: Reading — choosing between close options and filling a summary
goal: Mengeliminasi tiga opsi salah di soal pilihan ganda dengan alasan yang bisa disebut, dan mengisi ringkasan dengan kelas kata yang tepat, baik memakai bank kata maupun tanpa.
bekal: membaca stem lebih dulu dan menemukan kalimat sumbernya sebelum melihat opsi
menamai jenis kesalahan tiap opsi yang kamu coret
menebak kelas kata yang hilang di ringkasan sebelum menengok teks

sections.title: Multiple choice: yang diuji bukan pemahaman, tapi kesabaran

blocks.text: Soal pilihan ganda Reading punya empat opsi, dan tiga di antaranya dirancang oleh orang yang tahu persis bagaimana kamu akan salah. Semua opsi memakai kosakata dari passage, semuanya terdengar masuk akal, dan biasanya dua opsi bertahan sampai akhir. Kalau kamu memilih dengan cara membaca opsi lalu bertanya *apa ini terdengar benar*, kamu memilih dengan cara yang paling mudah dijebak.

items: **Baca stem-nya saja dulu — tutup opsinya.** Stem adalah pertanyaan atau awal kalimatnya. Pahami apa yang ditanyakan sebelum otakmu diberi empat pilihan yang membingungkan.

**Temukan lokasinya di passage.** Soal MCQ mengikuti urutan passage, jadi jawaban soal 3 pasti ada di antara jawaban soal 2 dan soal 4. Kalau kamu sudah mengerjakan kelompok soal lain, sebagian besar pekerjaan ini sudah selesai.
**Baca kalimat sumbernya, lalu jawab sendiri dengan kata-katamu.** Baru buka opsinya dan cari yang paling dekat dengan jawabanmu.
**Coret satu per satu, dan sebutkan alasannya.** Kalau kamu tidak bisa menyebut kenapa sebuah opsi salah, kamu belum mencoret apa pun — kamu baru merasa.
**Kalau tersisa dua, cari SATU kata yang membedakan.** Biasanya kata pembatas: *all, only, most, always, mainly, first*. Perbedaannya hampir tidak pernah ada di gagasan besarnya.

blocks.title: Empat jenis opsi salah — hafalkan namanya
items: **Terlalu ekstrem.** Memakai *never, always, all, impossible, must*, padahal passage berkata *often, tends to, in most cases*. Passage akademik jarang berbicara mutlak; opsi yang berbicara mutlak hampir selalu salah.

**Benar tapi bukan jawabannya.** Pernyataan yang memang ada di passage, tapi tidak menjawab stem. Ini pengecoh yang paling banyak memakan korban, karena kamu bisa membuktikan bahwa isinya benar. Kembali ke stem dan tanyakan: apakah ini MENJAWAB pertanyaannya?
**Kata dari teks, makna berbeda.** Menyalin frasa mencolok dari passage lalu menukar pelaku, waktu, atau arah hubungannya. Kata yang kamu kenali adalah umpan.
**Setengah benar.** Bagian pertama opsi cocok, bagian keduanya tidak. Baca opsi sampai titiknya, jangan berhenti saat sudah terasa cocok.

sections.title: Summary completion: dua versi, dua cara kerja

blocks.text: Ringkasan (summary) adalah parafrase satu bagian passage — kadang seluruhnya, lebih sering hanya dua atau tiga paragraf — dengan beberapa lubang. Ada dua versi, dan cara mengerjakannya berbeda.

head: Aspek
Dengan bank kata (A–J)
Tanpa bank kata
rows: Sumber jawaban
Daftar kata di kotak, biasanya 8–12 pilihan
Kata PERSIS dari passage
Yang ditulis di lembar jawaban
HURUF pilihan, bukan katanya
Kata itu sendiri, dengan ejaan benar
Jebakan utama
Beberapa pilihan adalah sinonim yang salah kelas kata
Batas kata dan bentuk kata
Langkah pertama
Tebak KELAS KATA tiap lubang
Tebak kelas kata, lalu scan kalimat sumbernya
Kabar baik
Jawabannya pasti ada di daftar — tak perlu ejaan
Tidak ada sinonim yang membingungkan
Kabar buruk
Pilihan pengecoh sengaja terasa cocok maknanya
Jawaban salah kalau kamu memakai katamu sendiri

blocks.text: Sebelum melihat teks maupun daftar kata, baca kalimat ringkasannya dan tentukan apa yang hilang. *Sounds that keep changing disturb our memory for ____* menuntut **kata benda**. *____ tasks are done faster with music* menuntut **kata sifat**. *Being able to ____ the music* menuntut **kata kerja bentuk dasar**. Langkah dua detik ini biasanya menghapus separuh isi bank kata sebelum kamu membaca satu barisnya.

blocks.title: Pengecoh favorit di MCQ dan summary
items: **Sinonim dengan kelas kata salah.** Bank kata memuat *alertness* dan *alert*, atau *choice* dan *choose*. Maknanya kamu tahu; yang diuji apakah kamu memasang yang cocok dengan tata bahasanya.
**Kata yang benar di lubang yang salah.** Ringkasan biasanya mengikuti urutan passage. Kalau lubang 4 kamu isi dari paragraf yang letaknya sebelum lubang 3, curigai.

**Ringkasan yang mencakup hanya sebagian passage.** Judul ringkasan sering menyebut paragrafnya, misalnya *Complete the summary of paragraphs C–E*. Mencari jawaban di paragraf lain adalah cara paling rapi untuk menghabiskan lima menit.
**Kata pembatas yang berpindah.** Passage berkata *usually*, opsi MCQ berkata *always*. Satu kata, satu poin.
**Opsi yang mengulang stem.** Kalau sebuah opsi hanya menyatakan ulang pertanyaannya dengan kata lain tanpa menambah informasi, biasanya itu bukan jawabannya.

blocks.text: Kalimat sumber: *"Although the sample was small and the advantage had gone within a quarter of an hour, the finding was reported around the world as proof that classical music makes children more intelligent."*
Stem: *What does the writer suggest about the way the study was reported?*

head: Opsi
Nilai
Jenis kesalahannya
rows: (A) The study should never have been published.
Salah
**Terlalu ekstrem.** Penulis mengkritik pemberitaannya, bukan penerbitannya. Tidak ada satu pun kata di teks yang mendukung penilaian sekeras itu.
(B) The sample used in the study was small.
Salah
**Benar tapi bukan jawabannya.** Kalimatnya memang menyebut *the sample was small* — dan itulah kenapa opsi ini berbahaya. Tapi stem menanyakan soal PEMBERITAAN, bukan soal metodenya.
(C) The reports claimed far more than the findings supported.
**Benar**

*reported around the world as proof that…* berhadapan dengan *the sample was small* dan *the advantage had gone within a quarter of an hour*. Kata *Although* di awal kalimat adalah tanda bahwa penulis sedang menunjukkan jarak antara temuan dan klaim.
(D) The study proved that classical music makes children more intelligent.
Salah

**Kata dari teks, makna berbeda.** Frasa ini disalin utuh dari kalimat sumber, tetapi di teks itu adalah isi klaim media, bukan temuan penelitian. Menyalin frasa terpanjang yang kamu kenali adalah kebiasaan yang mahal.

blocks.text: Kalimat sumber yang sama bisa dipakai untuk lubang ringkasan: *The 1993 result was widely reported as ____ that music improves intelligence.* Kelas kata yang dibutuhkan: kata benda. Jawabannya *proof* — satu kata, persis dari teks. Perhatikan bahwa MCQ menuntutmu menilai maksud penulis, sementara lubang ringkasan hanya menuntutmu menyalin dengan cermat. Dua keterampilan berbeda dari satu kalimat yang sama.
Skim 2–3 menit, lalu kerjakan Latihan 1–3. Bank kata untuk Latihan 2 ada di bagian berikutnya. Target: **20 menit** untuk 13 soal.

blocks.title: Does Background Music Help You Work?

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: In 1993 a one-page report in a psychology journal described thirty-six university students who listened to ten minutes of a Mozart sonata and then performed better on a test of spatial reasoning than students who had waited in silence. The students had been assessed on a single narrow task, folding and cutting paper in the mind's eye, and the advantage had gone within about fifteen minutes. None of this survived contact with the newspapers. The finding was reported around the world as proof that classical music makes children more intelligent, at least one government distributed recordings to new parents, and a small industry grew up around what became known as the Mozart effect. A review published in 2010, covering forty later experiments, did find a small and genuine advantage, but it vanished whenever the comparison group listened to something else they enjoyed, such as an audiobook.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: That last detail is the whole explanation. What the music had improved was not spatial ability but the listener: people who have just heard something they like are more awake and in a better mood, and awake people in a good mood do slightly better at almost everything for a short while. Psychologists call this the arousal-and-mood account, and it has held up well. It also predicts something the newspapers found less appealing: if a student prefers loud guitar music to Mozart, the guitar music will produce the same effect. There is nothing in the structure of a sonata that reorganises the brain.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Arousal, however, is only half of the story, because sound also competes for attention. Laboratory work on what is called the irrelevant sound effect shows that memory for the order of items collapses when the background contains sound that keeps changing, while a steady, unvarying tone does almost no damage. Words are the worst intruders of all, which is why an overheard conversation is harder to work through than traffic noise at the same volume. In one experiment, participants proofreading a legal contract missed almost a fifth more errors when a familiar song with lyrics was playing than when the same song was played as an instrumental arrangement.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: It follows that the useful question is not whether music helps, but which task is being done. Repetitive work with a low mental load, such as sorting items on a production line or entering figures into a database, is generally completed faster and reported as less tiresome when music is playing, because the music supplies arousal that the task itself cannot. Work that loads the working memory, such as writing an argument, learning a sequence, or reading anything that must be held in mind sentence by sentence, is measurably worse with music than in silence. The same headphones can therefore help in the morning and hinder in the afternoon.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Individuals differ as well, and along a line that surprises people. Introverts, who on most measures already sit at a higher level of baseline cortical arousal, are more disrupted by background sound than extroverts, who often perform better with it. Trained musicians are also disturbed more than other listeners by instrumental music, apparently because they cannot help analysing what they hear. Age plays a part too: the ability to filter out irrelevant sound weakens steadily after the age of about fifty. None of these differences is large enough to justify a rule for a whole office, which is precisely the problem employers face.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Open-plan offices have made the question commercial. Since intelligible speech is the single most disruptive sound in a workplace, many employers now play quiet instrumental music to mask the sound of nearby conversations, on the argument that a predictable sound is easier to ignore than an unpredictable one. A study of four offices in which such systems were installed found that employees rated their own concentration as clearly better afterwards, while objective measures of their output did not change at all. Whether that counts as success depends on what the employer was buying.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The research, taken together, points to something less exciting than a shortcut to intelligence and more useful in practice. Silence remains the safest condition for anything genuinely difficult. Familiar instrumental music, played quietly, is a reasonable companion for work that is dull rather than demanding, and familiarity matters because a track you already know demands nothing. Most consistently of all, being able to choose the music yourself appears to matter more than the music itself: in study after study, people given control over their own sound environment outperform people given the same sound without a say in it.

blocks.title: List of Words
items: **A** alertness · **B** speech · **C** repetitive · **D** order · **E** silence
**F** volume · **G** familiar · **H** musicians · **I** complex · **J** mood

blocks.text: Sepuluh kata untuk lima lubang. Tulis **hurufnya**, bukan katanya. Sebelum melihat daftar ini lagi, tandai dulu kelas kata yang dibutuhkan tiap lubang di Latihan 2 — tiga di antaranya menuntut kata benda tunggal, satu kata sifat, dan satu kata benda jamak.

exercises.prompt: Questions 1–5. Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. — Artinya: pilih huruf yang benar, A, B, C, atau D.
items: What does the writer say about the 1993 study? (A) Its results have never been reproduced. (B) It measured a wider range of abilities than was later claimed. (C) It was summarised accurately by the press. (D) The advantage it recorded did not last long. ____

According to the arousal-and-mood account, why did the students do better? (A) Because a sonata has a particular mathematical structure. (B) Because they were more awake and in a better mood. (C) Because they had practised the task beforehand. (D) Because they were tested in a quieter room. ____

What did the proofreading experiment show about lyrics? (A) They helped readers who already knew the song. (B) They made no difference to accuracy. (C) They interfered more than the same music without words. (D) They slowed readers only when the music was unfamiliar. ____

Which task is most likely to be done better with music playing? (A) Writing an argument. (B) Sorting items on a production line. (C) Learning a sequence of items in order. (D) Reading a contract closely. ____

What did the study of four open-plan offices find? (A) Output rose by almost a fifth. (B) Staff felt they concentrated better although their output was unchanged. (C) Headphones proved more effective than a music system. (D) Speech was less disruptive than instrumental music. ____

exercises.prompt: Questions 6–10. Complete the summary of paragraphs C–E below. Choose the correct letter, A–J, from the List of Words above. — Artinya: lengkapi ringkasan paragraf C–E di bawah. Pilih huruf yang benar, A–J, dari List of Words di atas.
items: Sound that keeps changing damages our memory for ____ , whereas an unvarying tone does very little harm.
Words are the most intrusive sound of all, so ____ is the hardest kind of background noise to work through.
____ work with a low mental load is usually finished faster when music is playing.
Tasks that load the working memory, on the other hand, are done best in ____ .
Among listeners, trained ____ are disturbed more than most by instrumental music.

exercises.prompt: Questions 11–13. Complete the summary of paragraphs F–G below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. — Artinya: lengkapi ringkasan paragraf F–G di bawah. Ambil SATU KATA SAJA dari bacaan untuk tiap jawaban.
items: In open-plan offices, quiet instrumental music is played in order to ____ the sound of nearby conversations.
For work that is genuinely difficult, the safest condition remains ____ .
Above all, being able to ____ the music yourself matters more than which music is played.

head: No
Jawaban
Kalimat sumber & alasan
rows: D

Par. A: *the advantage had gone within about fifteen minutes*. Opsi A salah karena par. A justru berkata review 2010 *did find a small and genuine advantage*. Opsi B kebalikannya: *a single narrow task*. Opsi C dibantah *None of this survived contact with the newspapers*.
B

Par. B: *people who have just heard something they like are more awake and in a better mood*. Opsi A adalah **kata dari teks, makna berbeda** — par. B menutup dengan *There is nothing in the structure of a sonata that reorganises the brain*, jadi struktur musik justru dibantah.
C

Par. C: *missed almost a fifth more errors when a familiar song with lyrics was playing than when the same song was played as an instrumental arrangement*. Opsi D memakai kata *familiar* dari kalimat yang sama, tetapi membalik arahnya: lagunya justru sudah dikenal.
B

Par. D: *sorting items on a production line or entering figures into a database, is generally completed faster*. Tiga opsi lain semuanya disebut di paragraf yang sama sebagai contoh tugas yang MEMBURUK dengan musik — pengecoh **setengah benar** yang hanya bisa dipilah dengan membaca seluruh paragraf, bukan sekadar mengenali kata.
B

Par. F: *employees rated their own concentration as clearly better afterwards, while objective measures of their output did not change at all*. Opsi A memungut *almost a fifth* dari paragraf C — angka yang benar dari penelitian yang salah. Opsi D membalik kalimat *intelligible speech is the single most disruptive sound*.
D (order)
Par. C: *memory for the order of items collapses when the background contains sound that keeps changing*. Lubangnya menuntut kata benda setelah *memory for*.
B (speech)

Par. C: *Words are the worst intruders of all, which is why an overheard conversation is harder to work through*. *Speech* adalah bentuk umum dari *an overheard conversation*, dan par. F menegaskannya: *intelligible speech is the single most disruptive sound*.
C (repetitive)

Par. D: *Repetitive work with a low mental load … is generally completed faster*. Lubang di awal kalimat, di depan kata benda *work* — yang dibutuhkan kata sifat. Pengecoh *complex* juga kata sifat, tetapi maknanya kebalikan.
E (silence)
Par. D: *is measurably worse with music than in silence*. Ringkasan membalik kalimatnya (*done best in silence*), jadi maknanya sama.
H (musicians)
Par. E: *Trained musicians are also disturbed more than other listeners by instrumental music*. Kata *Trained* sudah tercetak di ringkasan, jadi yang hilang kata bendanya.
mask

Par. F: *many employers now play quiet instrumental music to mask the sound of nearby conversations*. Setelah *in order to*, yang dibutuhkan kata kerja bentuk dasar — dan teksnya memang *mask*. *Masking* ditolak karena mengubah bentuk kata.
silence
Par. G: *Silence remains the safest condition for anything genuinely difficult.* Batasnya ONE WORD ONLY, jadi *complete silence* salah walaupun terdengar wajar.
choose

Par. G: *being able to choose the music yourself appears to matter more than the music itself*. *Control* muncul di kalimat berikutnya dan sering dipilih, tetapi tata bahasanya tidak cocok: *being able to control* memang mungkin, namun kalimat ringkasan meniru kalimat sumber, dan kata yang dipakai di sana adalah *choose*.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari passage ini
items: Soal 5 memperlihatkan pengecoh angka yang paling licik: *almost a fifth* betul-betul ada di passage, tetapi di paragraf C tentang proofreading, bukan di paragraf F tentang kantor. Saat sebuah opsi memuat angka, periksa apakah angkanya berada di paragraf yang sedang ditanyakan.

Di Latihan 2, dua pengecoh (*alertness*, *mood*) adalah kata kunci paragraf B — bagian passage yang TIDAK diringkas. Instruksi menyebut *paragraphs C–E*, dan mematuhi batas itu langsung menghapus dua pilihan.

Latihan 3 menuntut kata kerja bentuk dasar dua kali (*mask*, *choose*). Menebak kelas kata sebelum melihat teks membuat kedua jawaban itu hampir tidak mungkin salah bentuk — dan bentuk kata adalah penyebab kehilangan poin nomor satu di soal isian.
